name: BD-JB-13.42 - missing checkPackageAccess check on PS5

root_cause.summary: PS5 13.42's BD-J checkPackageAccess omits a check that is present in 13.60. The gap lets an Xlet use sun.launcher.LauncherHelper and export a custom jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe class, escaping the Java sandbox without the earlier BDJO path traversal. Gezine found it by diffing the PS5 13.42 and 13.60 BD-J modules.
root_cause.primitive: missing authorization check in BD-J checkPackageAccess, allowing a custom jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe class to be exported
root_cause.trigger: BD-J Xlet on a burned Blu-ray on PS5 13.42 or below
root_cause.consequence: Java sandbox escape to native userland code execution

discovery_approach.summary: Gezine diffed the PS5 13.42 and 13.60 BD-J modules in 2026 and found the missing check in checkPackageAccess. He implemented the variant in BD-JB5 (commit 4c28ff2, 2026-08-04), extending the exploit's support to 13.42; 13.60 is the first fixed release.
signals: checkPackageAccess differs between the 13.42 and 13.60 BD-J modules
sun.launcher.LauncherHelper and jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe references in the Xlet
a package-access check that is present in 13.60 but absent in 13.42

differences: 13.60 adds the missing check in checkPackageAccess; Gezine found it by diffing the 13.42 and 13.60 BD-J modules (PS5 wiki).
13.60 also breaks BD-JB5's stock path; on 13.60+ BD-J requires bdj_unpatch.elf from an already-jailbroken console, which backs up and replaces bdjstack.jar (BD-JB5 README).

patch_evidence.what: the PS5 dev wiki records the 13.42-to-13.60 BD-J module diff and the missing check; BD-JB5's README records the 13.42 support ceiling and the 13.60+ workaround
patch_evidence.limits: no firmware bytes and no quoted patched function are stored or linked here

sources.supports: BD-JB-13.42 at PS5 <=13.42, the missing check in checkPackageAccess, sun.launcher.LauncherHelper plus jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe, discovery by diffing 13.42/13.60, fixed in 13.60
PS5 BD-J sandbox escape supported up to 13.42; on 13.60+ it needs an already-jailbroken PS5 and bdj_unpatch.elf, which backs up and replaces bdjstack.jar
the BD-JB-EX system_ex injection context (PS4 <=13.52 / PS5 <=13.60) that explains why 13.60+ still has a BD-J path once a kernel exploit exists

a BD-J kernel payload implemented as Java (com.bdjb.exploit.kernel.ExploitNetControlImpl) that dlsyms libkernel symbols and drives __sys_netcontrol, showing the BD-J entry can directly carry a netcontrol kernel exploit

gaps: The wiki's bug description is one sentence; no full technical writeup of the 13.42 chain was fetched.
The exact checkPackageAccess condition and the LauncherHelper call sequence are not quoted.
BD-JB5 supports 'up to 13.42', but versions between 13.42 and 13.60 are not enumerated in the fetched sources.
